correctness.rationale: An explicit, reproducible 13^3 matrix computation gives A^28=I+169B with B mod13=[[6,6],[6,7]]. For all positive d the matrix binomial remainder after dividing U^d-I by 169d is divisible by13. For every r, the unit coefficient is 6(P_(r+1)-P_r) mod13; it cannot vanish because the Pell norm then forces the nonsquare 6 or 7 modulo13. Therefore the pairwise exact valuation is 2+nu13(u-v), making every 28-index branch a bijection onto its 169-coset at each level. Direct recurrence seed residues have multiplicity 4 for 0 and 2 for each other one, giving image cardinality 13^(k-1). The norm identity, period minimality, infinity of occurrence and normalized Haar measure are separately proved. Finite checker was successfully executed for levels1..6 and 1,120 differences; it is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The smallest Pell-Wieferich prime 13 is naturally exceptional because its prime-square recurrence period does not expand. The result completely classifies the natural scalar residue spectrum for every 13-power; gives the sharp image-size and 13-adic Haar measure 1/13; proves an exact nonuniform 4/2 fiber law and an index-branch isometry that explains all levels. This is a meaningful infinite natural invariant, not a routine modular lookup or arbitrary parameter substitution.
